headlines.title: 1 dead, 6 hurt following shooting at Solano Town Center in Fairfield
headlines.description: One person died and six others were hurt following a shooting at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield on Friday night, according to police. Officers responded to a shooting inside the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store at 8:30 p.m., authorities said. Fairfield police said seven people were shot and one of them died. The other six victims were taken to the hospital, and three of them are in critical condition. Police said the suspect has not been identified. This is an ongoing investigation. Suisun City mayor Alma Hernandez released a statement regarding the incident. “Our thoughts are with the City of Fairfield tonight. Reports of an active shooter at Solano Town Center (Fairfield Mall) have left multiple victims. Law enforcement is actively searching for the suspect. Our Suisun City Police Department is supporting the search through mutual aid. “Although this happened in Fairfield, it is close to our community, so please stay alert and use official sources for the latest information. For updates, follow the Fairfield, CA Police Department on Facebook and the City of Fairfield’s official websites and social media accounts. Please avoid sharing unverified posts, which can spread confusion and hinder the response. “Please join us in praying for the victims and their families, and for the officers working to bring the suspect into custody. “Once this incident is resolved, we will need to come together as a community to support each other, the victims, and everyone affected by this tragedy. We will refer to the City of Fairfield Police Department to share more information as it becomes available.” This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. headlines.title: Sheriff's office restricts access to South Bay jail following ICE activity
headlines.description: ICE officers have maintained a constant presence this week, especially around Santa Clara County’s jail facilities, apparently waiting to question people about their immigration status right after they’re released. This has led to some physical confrontations caught on camera. NBC Bay Area was inside the Elmwood facility on Friday before the sheriff’s office announced that access to the parking lot and lobby would be restricted to people with direct business at the facility. The restrictions come as a response to the increased ICE activity, including an incident in which officers used a taser. Liz Gonzalez was shooting video of a man released from the Elmwood jail who tried to elude ICE officers by hiding in a nearby creek. He ran and green lights from tasers were aimed right at him. “Obviously I was in fear. I was shocked. I was surprised and scared by what I saw. I was so scared for those individuals because I thought that they were going to kill them,” Gonzalez said. Gonzalez is with the watchdog group Silicon Valley De-Bug, which has been videotaping ICE officers since Sunday when they showed up at Elmwood, capturing encounters with people being released. The Rapid Response Network in Santa Clara County says ICE officers have been very assertive. Top Santa Clara County leaders said on Friday they are very concerned about the escalation in activity, stating, “The county continues to uphold its long-standing non-cooperation policies regarding federal civil immigration enforcement. With Election Day next week, we are committed to ensuring all citizens are able to freely and safely cast their vote.” “Well, it’s no coincidence that we’ve seen a larger ICE presence right before the elections, so this is very consistent with what we’re seeing up and down the state of California,” Rapid Response Network coordinator Jeremy Barousse said. For now, groups say the immigrant community is on edge. “People are afraid. Both family members outside, and we’re hearing that the people detained inside also very afraid. Even folks who are ‘not at risk.’ Everybody’s at risk, and especially people who look Latino, obviously we know that,” Gonzalez said.

headlines.title: Star witness in Sheng Thao corruption trial details alleged bribery scheme
headlines.description: The star prosecution witness in the federal corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao testified Friday about his role in an alleged scheme to funnel money to her in exchange for political favors. Mario Juarez, a long-time Oakland political operative and former City Council candidate, testified about how he allegedly managed a pay-to-play relationship between Thao, her romantic partner Andre Jones, and David and Andy Duong, a father-son duo who operate the city’s recycling contractor, California Waste Solutions. Thao, Jones and the Duongs all pleaded not guilty to a rash of federal corruption and bribery charges in January. Juarez is testifying for the U.S. Department of Justice after pleading guilty to a bribery conspiracy charge of his own. In court on Friday, Juarez detailed the accusations at the heart of the prosecution’s case — that the Duongs allegedly agreed to pay Jones $300,000 a year for a fake job in exchange for Thao’s help securing a city contract to purchase modular homes. The homes were to be built by a company called Evolutionary Homes, founded by Juarez and the Duongs to build modular housing units out of old shipping containers with the intention of selling them to local governments to help with homelessness issues. Sheng Thao Oct 29 Sheng Thao Oct 28 The alleged quid pro quo agreement also involved Thao helping the family win a 10-year extension for their existing recycling contract, an extension of their existing land-lease at the old Oakland army base and an alleged promise from Thao to place their hand-picked candidate in a high-level position inside city government. Juarez also told the jury that as part of the illicit agreement, he helped the Duongs spend $75,000 on last-minute negative campaign mailers to help Thao win a tight mayoral election in 2022. He also said that he illegally coordinated with Jones to design the mailers. The original agreement only included using an independent expenditure committee to produce the negative mailers and to help Thao get elected, Juarez said, but Thao allegedly had an additional demand. “Then she threw a curveball,” he said. “We were willing to do the campaign and all the things in exchange, but she said, ‘I want $300,000 in exchange.'” The defendants were then thrust into a position in which they had to figure out a way to make payments to Jones look legitimate, Juarez said. To do that, they allegedly created a fake, no-show job for Jones so the payments wouldn’t arouse suspicion, Juarez said. During the day’s testimony, lead prosecutor Assistant U.S. Attorney Abraham Fine showed the jury images of checks written to Jones that were allegedly in exchange for Thao’s part in the conspiracy. The jury also saw dozens of text messages between the defendants that prosecutors say are evidence of their long-running effort to pull off the scheme. In one such exchange after Thao eked out a narrow win in the mayoral election, Juarez texted Andy Duong “so we may go to jail.” “I was making light that we just committed a crime by funding an election and we may go to jail for doing this crime, but we’ll have $100 million in our bank account,” Jaurez told the jury Friday. Juarez also testified that the payments to Jones were going to increase to a total of up to $3 million, based on how many modular homes Oakland agreed to buy, “in exchange” for Thao’s agreement to help with the Duongs’ list of requests. “In exchange, the compensation went from $300,000 to a structure that would now make them millionaires,” Juarez said. He also testified about how he and Andy Duong planned their communications between themselves and other people involved in the alleged conspiracy in order to protect Andy’s father, David, and so that the elder Duong would have “plausible deniability” in the event that law enforcement started poking around. Juarez also said that he and Andy Duong became frustrated as the deal started to fall apart and when it appeared as of Thao wasn’t holding up her part of the bargain. “We didn’t invest money, talent, (negative political) ‘hits,’ took the time out of our day because we liked Sheng Thao,” he said, adding that they did all those things so that she would help them execute the scheme to further their business interests. Juarez testified for several hours Friday and is expected to be back on the stand when the trial resumes Thursday.

headlines.title: 2 San Jose women allegedly stabbed person to death, dumped body in rural Alameda County
headlines.description: Two San Jose women were arrested earlier this week on suspicion of killing a person whose body was found in August off the side of a rural road in eastern Alameda County, police said Friday. Alexia Nieves Solache, 22, and Veronica Rangel, 55, allegedly stabbed the unidentified victim to death at a home in San Jose before dumping their body in the area of Tesla and Eagles Run roads outside Livermore, according to police. Alameda County Sheriff’s Office deputies initially responded at about 3:04 p.m. on Aug. 25 to the area of Tesla and Eagles Run roads to investigate a report of a possible deceased person, San Jose police said. The reporting party said he was driving when he spotted what appeared to be a concealed person in a ravine. Responding sheriff’s deputies found the person and determined they were dead. The victim had suffered multiple stab wounds, and their manner of death was ruled a homicide, according to police. Deputies determined the victim was last seen on Aug. 22 at a home on the 700 block of North Seventh Street in San Jose. The home did not belong to the victim, police said. Deputies also identified a suspect vehicle that was seen traveling from the home in San Jose to the location outside Livermore where the victim was found. Investigators determined the homicide happened at the home in San Jose, and they identified Solache and Rangel as the primary suspects, police said. Both suspects were arrested on Tuesday – Solache in Los Angeles and Rangel in San Jose, according to police. They were eventually booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of murder. The motive and circumstances surrounding the homicide – San Jose’s 24th of 2026 – remain under investigation, police said. Anyone with information is asked to contact San Jose police Detective Sgt. Varela and/or Detective Montoya by email at 3638@sanjoseca.gov and/or 3644@sanjoseca.gov or by phone at 408-277-5283.

headlines.title: Newsom renames California labor building after Dolores Huerta
headlines.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom is honoring the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta by putting her name on a state building. Newsom announced Friday he will rename the new California Labor and Workforce Development Agency Building in Sacramento after the pioneer. After Huerta’s passing this week, Newsom issued a statement, saying, “We owe her an immeasurable debt of gratitude for her tireless advocacy…and every person who walks through the doors of the building will be reminded of her enduring legacy and the mission she left for us all.” The new building officially opened at the start of this year. Civil Rights Oct 28 In Memoriam Oct 28 In Memoriam Oct 29 Worker rights pioneer Dolores Huerta wanted others to feel seen

headlines.title: Newsom highlights California's homelessness efforts during Marin County visit
headlines.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom spoke in Marin County Friday morning about a new milestone in reducing homelessness in California and expanding access to behavioral health services. The Ritter Center in San Rafael is celebrating a new $14 million health and wellness center as a result of voter-enacted Proposition 1. The center will increase capacity by 25% and put case management, housing support, food assistance and other services under one roof. Newsom said the public needs to know that the investment voters made by voting yes on the bond measure is paying off. The full report is available in the video above.

headlines.title: San Francisco prepares for coastal flooding as high tides continue
headlines.description: Coastal flood advisories across the Bay Area have been extended into the weekend, with some communities pre-staging equipment in case they need to respond to flood-prone areas. NBC Bay Area meteorologists have warned that high tides could surge nearly 2 feet above normal, potentially causing problems for public transit in San Francisco, including Muni trains. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is preparing equipment, including tons of sandbags that crews can deploy as needed, large sump pumps that can be placed in flooded tunnels or submerged trouble spots, and generators to power those pumps. For Muni, two potential trouble spots are its light rail station at Cesar Chavez and Illinois streets, near flood-prone Islais Creek, and the Embarcadero Street Muni tunnel, which is close to an area along the Embarcadero that floods during high tide. “High priority for us is protecting subway service,” said John Becker, SFMTA’s acting chief infrastructure officer. “Obviously, it’s a huge link across the city and also in our shared station partnership with BART. It’s a huge regional impact we could have.” High tides have already caused flooding in Marin County this week, with low-lying areas near Mill Valley inundated since Monday. San Francisco’s Embarcadero has also flooded this week. Authorities in San Mateo County announced their flood staging plans Friday. There is only a slight chance of rain in San Francisco this weekend. The coastal flooding is happening because of unusually high tide conditions. Drivers are being reminded not to drive through flooded areas because it can be difficult to determine how deep or dangerous the water may be.

headlines.title: Wall Street drops to its worst day since June after the sell-off for tech stocks deepens
headlines.description: A sell-off for tech stocks got even worse Friday on worries that Wall Street’s frenzy around artificial-intelligence technology sent prices too high. The S&P 500 tumbled 1.8% for its worst day since June, and it closed out a third straight losing week. The weakness for technology stocks dragged the Nasdaq composite down a market-leading 2.9%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 572 points, or 1.1%. The U.S. stock market remains only 3.1% below its all-time high, which has boosted the value of workers’ 401(k) accounts, but it’s become increasingly shaky as Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States approach. Worries about AI in general have already become a concern for voters across political parties, and President Donald Trump has historically used the stock market’s performance as a measure of his own success. Intel’s stock led the way lower and plunged 28.6% for its worst drop since 1974. The chipmaker gave a forecast for profit in the final three months of this year that fell short of analysts’ expectations, as CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the personal-computer industry continues to feel pressure. The drop came even though Intel reported a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Amazon fell 1.4% after reporting a weaker profit for the summer than analysts expected. Potentially more concerning for investors was Amazon’s reporting that it burned through $42.4 billion of cash over the prior 12 months, according to a measure called free cash flow. It spent $94.8 billion on property and equipment, primarily through investments in artificial-intelligence technology. A day earlier, Alphabet’s stock dropped more than 12% to its worst day on record and dragged the S&P 500 down after telling investors it burned through more cash during the summer than the spring. The company behind Google and YouTube cited similar, mammoth investments in AI. Worries are rising about whether all the hundreds of billions of dollars will produce enough profit and productivity to make the investment worth it. At the same time, stocks of computer chip companies and other winners from the frenzy to build AI data centers have come under pressure on concerns that high interest rates may slow the further build out of data centers. “We’re moving out of the hopes and dreams phase of the AI trade and into the ‘show me’ phase,” said Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, in a note to investors. A drop of 4.2% for Nvidia, the chip company that became the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward, outweighing even Intel. In the cryptocurrency industry, meanwhile, stocks tumbled following a hack on the world’s biggest crypto exchange. The price of bitcoin fell below $77,000 from more than $86,000 earlier this month, and a U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm said a North Korean unit was likely behind the attack that impacted more than $6 billion worth of crypto at Binance. Coinbase Global fell 10.6% even though it reported stronger results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Strategy, which says it owns about 4% of the total supply of bitcoin, fell 7.8%. It also reported a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected, while saying its chief financial officer will resign next week for personal reasons. Outside of tech, stocks were more resilient as many rallied after reporting stronger profits for the summer than analysts expected. Nearly as many stocks rose within the S&P 500 index as fell. ExxonMobil climbed 2.2%, and Chevron added 1.8% after the oil giants reported stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected. Mondelez International rose 3.9% after the company behind Oreo cookies and Ritz crackers reported stronger-than-expected growth. Colgate-Palmolive climbed 2.3% after higher prices for its products around much of the world helped it deliver better revenue and profit than analysts expected. Expectations are high for U.S. companies’ ability to make bigger profits, even though people around the world are feeling discouraged about high inflation and high fuel prices. Such expectations are what drove the S&P 500 to its record earlier this month. All told, the S&P 500 fell 140.32 points to 7,580.07. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 572.25 to 51,770.31, and the Nasdaq composite sank 747.73 to 25,437.00. In the bond market, Treasury yields eased in a signal that investors were buying U.S. government bonds in search of something safer to own. The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.93% from 4.98% late Thursday and from more than 5.30% earlier in the month. Treasury yields fell even though oil prices bounced higher, something that usually drives yields upward because it worsens inflation. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 2.4% to $113.43. It’s near the high end of its range since the war with Iran sent oil prices and inflation higher. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed in Europe following sharper swings in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi dropped 3.5% as worries about AI hit its tech-heavy market, while the Hang Seng in Hong Kong climbed 1.5%. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.1% after the Bank of Japan decided to keep interest rates steady, echoing moves made earlier in the week by the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank. ___ AP Business Writers Yuri Kageyama and Michelle Chapman contributed to this report.

headlines.title: Contra Costa County hosts Halloween-themed wedding ‘scaremonies'
headlines.description: The Contra Costa County Clerk’s Office in Martinez is holding its annual Halloween-themed wedding ceremonies, known as “scaremonies,” Friday. Couples get married by county staff dressed in costume. Many couples and even their guests get into the Halloween spirit by dressing up. Some couples decided to go all out. A few appointments are still open, and walk-in couples will be accepted through 3:30 p.m. Friday. Couples will need to get a marriage license before the ceremony. They can purchase one during their appointment. Traditional ceremonies will still be available for those who prefer a more classic approach.

headlines.title: Bay Area real estate executive sentenced to 18 months for defrauding investors
headlines.description: A former Bay Area real estate executive was sentenced earlier this week to 18 months in federal prison for defrauding investors of more than $2.2 million, according to federal prosecutors. Sanjeev Acharya, 58, of San Jose, was sentenced Wednesday for wire fraud and a financial transaction involving money obtained through fraud, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said in a statement. Acharya was the president and CEO of SiliconSage Builders and related companies, which supported investments in large real estate developments across the Bay Area. He personally solicited investments to fund the projects, according to his plea agreement. Federal prosecutors said Acharya misled more than 20 investors between March and Oct. 26, 2020, by failing to disclose that SiliconSage was heavily in debt and facing serious cash flow problems. The company was struggling financially in part because of the COVID-19 pandemic and needed new investments to stay afloat, according to the plea agreement. The investors lost more than $2.2 million as a result of the fraud, prosecutors said. “Behind these losses are individuals and families whose retirement plans, educational opportunities, and financial security were put at risk,” said John Abram, acting special agent in charge of the IRS Criminal Investigation San Francisco Field Office. Acharya was charged in September 2025 and pleaded guilty in January 2026 to wire fraud and engaging in a monetary transaction involving property derived from fraud. Besides the prison sentence, Breyer ordered Acharya to serve two years of supervised release and pay $2.25 million in restitution to victims. Acharya is scheduled to begin serving his sentence on Jan. 9, 2027.

headlines.title: Coastal flooding expected to continue, rain possible across Bay Area
headlines.description: Moderate coastal flooding is possible along Bay Area shorelines through Sunday, while light rain could reach parts of the region Saturday, according to the National Weather Service. In an advisory early Friday, the weather service warned that high tides could flood low-lying areas, cause isolated road closures and contribute to coastal erosion. Rising water and waves could also reach farther up beaches than usual, making it harder for people to leave coastal areas safely. The coastal flooding risk extends along the shores of San Pablo, San Francisco and Monterey bays, as well as the Pacific coast. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to reach 1.9 feet above normal at 2:39 p.m. Friday. The level is forecast to reach 1.5 feet above normal on Saturday afternoon and a foot above normal on Sunday afternoon. At the Monterey tidal gauge, high tide is forecast to reach 1.8 feet above normal at 1:25 p.m. Friday. It is expected to reach 1.4 feet above normal Saturday and 0.8 feet above normal Sunday. The tide forecasts include about 1.5 feet of additional water from surge effects linked to thermal expansion and low pressure. High tide times can vary by as much as 90 minutes along the coast and throughout San Francisco Bay, forecasters said. Rain chances, meanwhile, are projected for Saturday, but the weather service said confidence remains low across much of the region. Most areas have a 10% to 30% chance of Halloween rain, with expected totals ranging from a few hundredths to about a tenth of an inch. Monterey County could see higher rain chances. The interior areas have a 50% to 70% probability of precipitation, while other areas in the two counties have a 30% to 50% chance. Rainfall totals could reach about a tenth to a third of an inch in the interior, forecasters said. The weather service said rain chances could return next week, with seasonal to slightly below seasonal temps expected through the extended forecast. Residents near the coast are advised to allow extra travel time because of possible road closures, avoid driving around barricades or through floodwaters of unknown depth, and take steps to protect property from flooding.
